newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks claw back big losses to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks claw back big losses to end firmer.

text.p: Swiss shares ended firmer and near the day's high after storming back from a slide of nearly 100 points on Friday.
"It was the biggest countermove I have ever seen," one trader said, adding that better-than-expected U.S. data and a recovery on Wall Street were instrumental in the late rise.
However, concern was seen growing over a possible U.S. interest rate hike. "We will continue to track U.S. markets closely," one dealer noted.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 26.3 points, or 0.57 percent, at 4,636.2 points. The day's high was at 4,637.6 points, the low at 4,513.5.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 12.27 points, or 0.42 percent, at 2,934.97.
SMI futures, which at first put pressure on the market, also recovered and gave stocks support, one trader noted. The March SMI contract added 18.6 points to 4,622.6.
A firming tendency in the U.S. dollar buoyed industrials.
Certificates of pharmaceutical Roche, which temporarily slid below the psychologically important level of 12,000 francs, ended with a jump of 180 francs, or 1.47 percent, to 12,435.
Other major pharmaceuticals and banks showed similar moves. Novartis just made it into positive terrain, adding one franc to 1,757.
Bourse newcomer Ciba Specialty Chemicals extended gains it posted at Thursday's bourse debut, powering ahead nine francs, or 7.73 percent, to 125.5 francs.
Sulzer was in the limelight after announcing plans to unify its share structure by converting participation certificates into registered shares. The shares added 12 francs to 977.
Dealers said Sulzer's drop in 1996 net profit to 82 million francs from 92 million was within market expectations. REUTRER
